name: iPhone18,3 (V57AP, T8150) / iOS 27.0 24A5424a / kernelcache.research.v57

identify._note: sha256 is of the DECOMPRESSED kernelcache, which is what insert_kext hashes to pick a config. `marker` is the fallback: it identifies the kernel build but not the exact image, so a marker-only match prints a warning and every address below should be re-derived before it is trusted.

slack._note: The 0x3ff8 of zeros at the end of __TEXT_EXEC is the com.apple.kernel fileset entry's __LAST segment, 0xfffffe000b36c000 + 0x4000, whose first 8 bytes are live code (msr SPSel,#1 ; ret) -- which is why the region starts at ...008 and why the size is identical across devices: it is a named, allocated segment, not incidental padding. r-x at runtime, so code runs there and nothing can be written to it.

build_tag._note: Both copies of the kernel version string carry a 19-character configuration field. Replacing it in place, at the same length, makes `uname -a` name exactly which image booted. The tag is RANDOM per build: two builds that happen to be byte-identical should still be distinguishable in a log.

symbols_note:
iOS kernelcaches export essentially nothing, so every entry here was recovered by hand.  See README.md, 'Porting to another kernelcache'.
sysctl_parent_children is &sysctl__debug_children, read out of the `debug` node's oid_arg1.  It reads 0 in a shipped image: the lists are built at boot.
scratch is WRITABLE kernel memory the kext needs for its one-shot guard and its sysctl_oid, because the kext's own memory is read-only.  0xfffffe000b6f0000 is inside a 0x40000-byte run of com.apple.kernel __DATA that was still zero a minute into boot, and a write there read back correctly and was restored.  CAVEAT: zero at t=60s is not proof the region is unowned -- it could be a buffer something fills in later -- so re-verify on a new image rather than inheriting this address.

oslog_extensible_paniclog._note: The 25 non-panic-path `BL _os_log_internal` sites that log 'Extensible paniclog not supported'. That message is emitted about every 3 s on this device, so the hook is known to fire, and the context is known safe for os_log because it was already calling it. The 26th site, 0xfffffe000b34b658, is in the panic path and is deliberately excluded.

sysent_table._note: 558 slots of 24 bytes, of which 15 still point at nosys.  The table lives in __DATA_CONST, so sy_call is NOT a plain VA: it is a DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64_KERNEL_CACHE link that the boot loader rebases and PAC-signs.  unix_syscall authenticates it with `blraa x8, x17`, x17 = 0xbcad, which is exactly the diversity the file already carries -- so a patch must KEEP the PAC fields and rewrite only the 30-bit target.  reference_slot 3 is read(2), an ordinary 3-argument syscall; its munger, sy_narg and sy_arg_bytes are copied verbatim so a patched slot has the shape of a syscall this kernel already dispatches.

extra_patches._note: Named single-instruction patches, applied with --extra NAME. Each names the bytes it expects to find, so a config that does not match the image fails the build instead of patching the wrong place.  None are shipped: what belongs here is specific to what you are doing.
